```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

_ = torch.manual_seed(481)
digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
x = torch.tensor(digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32) / 16
y = torch.tensor(digits[64].to_numpy())
n_train = 1200
order = torch.randperm(len(x))
x_train, y_train = x[order[:n_train]], y[order[:n_train]]
x_test, y_test = x[order[n_train:]], y[order[n_train:]]
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()


def make_mlp(seed=1):
    # A fresh copy of the digits MLP, with the same starting weights for a given seed.
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    return nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 10))


print(make_mlp())
```

The exercises use the `r format(nrow(py$digits), big.mark = ",")` digits of [`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv) [@alpaydin1998optdigits],
split as in the [feedforward networks chapter](feedforward-networks.qmd),
with `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` images in the [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set).
`make_mlp()` builds that chapter's [MLP](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-feedforward-network),
with the same starting weights each time,
so that every method below starts from the same place.
